subsystems.name: Bioink
subsystems.role: the printable living material — cells suspended in a gel that can flow through a nozzle and then set.

subsystems.name: Printer hardware
subsystems.role: deposits bioink in precise layers, often several materials at once.
parts: extrusion, inkjet, laser or light-sheet print heads

subsystems.name: Vascular network
subsystems.role: the channels that deliver oxygen and nutrients to cells more than about 1 mm from a surface.

subsystems.name: Support structure
subsystems.role: keeps soft printed tissue from collapsing while it matures.
parts: biodegradable polymer scaffold or support bath

subsystems.name: Perfusion bioreactor
subsystems.role: pumps warmed, oxygenated medium through the printed vessels so the tissue matures.

subsystems.name: Imaging and quality control
subsystems.role: checks that cells survived printing and vessels are patent before the tissue is used.
parts: imaging-derived 3D model for the print path

buildSteps.title: Obtain and expand cells
buildSteps.detail: A small biopsy or blood sample is reprogrammed to stem cells or expanded as primary cells in culture for weeks.

buildSteps.title: Formulate the bioink
buildSteps.detail: Cells are concentrated and mixed with a hydrogel that is liquid enough to print but holds shape afterwards.

buildSteps.title: Design the tissue
buildSteps.detail: CT, MRI or microscopy images become a 3D model, including a branching blood-vessel network sized to the cells' oxygen needs.

buildSteps.title: Print the tissue
buildSteps.detail: The printer lays down structural ink and sacrificial ink in alternating channels, layer by layer, inside a sterile enclosure.

buildSteps.title: Solidify and remove supports
buildSteps.detail: The gel is crosslinked by light, heat or ions, then the sacrificial ink is melted or dissolved away to leave hollow channels.

buildSteps.title: Line the vessels
buildSteps.detail: Endothelial cells are flowed into the channels and allowed to attach, forming a living lining.

buildSteps.title: Perfuse and mature
buildSteps.detail: The construct sits in a bioreactor for days to weeks with medium pumped through the channels, letting cells organise into tissue.

buildSteps.title: Test or implant
buildSteps.detail: The tissue is screened for viability and function, then used for drug testing or surgically implanted.

prerequisites.why: gives an expandable, patient-matched source of the many cell types a complex organ needs.

prerequisites.tech: Cell-compatible bioinks at high cell density
prerequisites.why: dense cell loads are what make printed tissue behave like tissue rather than a gel.
without perfused vessels, anything thicker than roughly a millimetre starves.
maturation and function only appear under continuous flow, not in a dish.
the vessel tree has to be computed and printed at the scale of individual cells.

pathway.milestone: printed skin, cartilage, cornea and bladder-shaped implants in early clinical use; printed tissue used for drug screening
pathway.unlocks: evidence that printed living tissue is safe, plus a market that funds the harder work.

pathway.milestone: vascularised tissue patches for liver, heart and kidney
pathway.unlocks: better drug testing and repair of damaged organs with the patient's own cells.

pathway.milestone: whole simple organs with lab-grown vessel trees, implanted in large-animal and first human studies
pathway.unlocks: an alternative to donor waiting lists.

pathway.milestone: on-demand, patient-specific organ printing in hospital-scale facilities
pathway.unlocks: replacement organs without lifelong immune suppression.
